findings.text: the comment this commit adds states the store's own window table is read in exactly one place (repeated in the pin case's docstring at 447 and in the commit body, and generalised there to 'an edit to the table lands as one named failure'), but the landing-record case reads TIER_WINDOW_SECONDS at 566-567 to build the minute and hour figures it then matches against the record; a mutation adding a third tier ('day': 86_400) to that table leaves the whole suite green (17 passed, exit 0, third_tier_added.log) even though the entry point now advertises it as a choice via choices=sorted(TIER_WINDOW_SECONDS), so an edit to the table is not always nought or one named failure; asserting set(_EXPECTED_TIER_GEOMETRY) == set(TIER_WINDOW_SECONDS) in the pin case and naming the record case as the second reader closes both halves, and neither changes what the code does.

item_verdicts.diff: read 2e3bb942..2d19be2b commit by commit -- 51 insertions and 10 deletions, all in tests/test_telemetry_store.py: the _EXPECTED_TIER_GEOMETRY table, the pin case that reads the store's table once, the tier parametrisation now taking window/rows/samples from the written table, the refusal case's code-2 and stderr assertions, and the two docstrings restated.  The only claims about behaviour reach the code through the entry point
item_verdicts.done_when: the reviewed head's full-file gate resolves green -- 17 passed in 9.51s, exit 0, on all_debug (baseline_gate.log) -- and the run's control logs replay to the same selections and outcomes (this review's controls/*.log).
item_verdicts.goal: both repairs red under mutation in every direction tried (11 mutation runs, each restored byte-exact with the module sha printed CLEAN in all of them).
item_verdicts.manifest: read at the head -- its tests line (17 passed) and its declared negative-control list of eleven were both checked, the eleven-name list is consistent with the logs on disk, and the four whose mutations it states verbatim reproduce exactly as recorded.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the commit's single path is the test file the run declares; no new condition is introduced by the test file that the diff at cf95ed36..2d19be2b and the tests bare-key registration need, which are consistent.

justifications.durability: each repaired case fails under the mutation it exists to catch, measured here rather than taken from the record: the refusal case under four status mutations and two reason mutations, the entry-point case in both directions (always-minute: [hour] fails 4320 == 72; always-hour: [minute] fails 72 == 4320), the record case under the record's own restated constant, and the tier geometry under the table mutation, where the one-place pin case is among the six failures (assert 1800 == 3600, alongside assert 144 == 72 at the hour parametrisation); docked because a table edit that adds a tier rather than moving one leaves every case green, which is the durability direction the commit's own claim covers and the suite does not.
justifications.evidence: every claim in the reviewed run's manifest that this node rests on was re-derived rather than read: the head's own full-file gate on all_debug is 17 passed in 9.51s, exit 0 (baseline_gate.log), matching its tests line; the module under test is byte-identical to the reviewed run's recorded revert target (sha256 ae60b6bf99239c63dc445d92b1c82a70703cbcf4ecdad8f10ca4aa30a2b4b12c, printed CLEAN by every restore); all four controls this commit declares were replayed from their verbatim mutations to the same red selections, and five further declared controls from earlier rounds were replayed the same way; the table mutation was measured at full-file width rather than at the four cases the recorded control used, giving 6 failed 11 passed (window_hour_1800.log); docked because the three oldest control logs (counter rule, null rule, successor readback) were not replayed -- their mutations are recorded as prose rather than as a line pair, so a replay would have been a new mutation of this review's rather than a replay.
justifications.fit: the additions follow the file's idiom -- a table of written geometry beside the fixture constants, a single parametrised case, why-first docstrings, and a doctest-free helper -- and the three naming checks over the commit's added lines return no hit; the tier comment's 'stayed green while TIER_HOUR moved from 3600 to 1800' states the mechanism the table exists for rather than a bug reference, which is the form the naming rules ask for.
justifications.goal: the two holes the previous round measured are closed in substance: the refusal case no longer accepts any SystemExit, and the entry-point case no longer computes its expectations from the table it exists to hold.
justifications.goal_fidelity: both repairs this commit names are delivered and measured under mutation of this review's own: the refusal case reddens on the status for a bare SystemExit (assert None == 2), for SystemExit(1) (assert 1 == 2) and for SystemExit(0) (assert 0 == 2), and on the reason for a silent exit 2 (assert '--tier' in '') and for an unrelated exit-2 failure that names --source instead (assert '--tier' in "usage: telemetry_store.py [-h] --source SOURCE...argument --source: invalid choice: 'second')) -- so an unrelated crash that exits with the same code is separated by the argument and value the reason names; and the entry-point case no longer moves with the table, failing with assert 144 == 72 on its own literal under TIER_HOUR 3600 -> 1800 while the minute parametrisation passes; docked because the invariant the same commit states beside the repair -- that the store's table is read in exactly one place -- is false at 566-567 and fails in the added-tier direction.
justifications.scope_discipline: 2d19be2b touches one file (git show --stat: tests/test_telemetry_store.py, 51 insertions and 10 deletions), which the reviewed run's manifest declares; the added lines carry no plan label, ticket reference, version suffix or author attribution under the three naming checks; and the link the added comment states.
